case_prompt:
A 49-year-old man presented with a 1-week history of pain in the right laterocervical region over the carotid bifurcation. The pain was a severe dull discomfort radiating to the ipsilateral ear and was triggered by head and neck movements. He had mild fever, fatigue, and myalgia at the onset but denied migraine or other neurological symptoms.

On examination, he was afebrile and in good general condition. There was localized swelling and tenderness at the right carotid bifurcation, worsened by palpation. No carotid bruits were audible. There was no cervical lymphadenopathy or induration along the jugular vein.

Laboratory studies showed a white-cell count of 9910/mm3, C-reactive protein of 0.10 mg%, and an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 20 mm/h. All other laboratory parameters were within normal limits.

Ultrasonography of the neck demonstrated an asymmetric hypoechoic thickening of the right distal common carotid artery extending into the proximal internal carotid artery. No intimal plaque or stenosis was present, and Doppler studies showed normal flow parameters. The thyroid, parathyroid, and salivary glands appeared normal; no neck mass or cervical lymphadenopathy was seen.

MRI of the neck revealed a thin rim of hyperintense tissue surrounding the right carotid artery on STIR sequences, which showed diffusion restriction on DWI and marked enhancement after contrast administration. There was no significant luminal narrowing.

diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Carotid dissection was excluded — “MRI is particularly useful in differentiating TIPIC syndrome from intramural hematoma or carotid dissection, that are the principal vascular differential diagnoses.” 2. Intramural hematoma was excluded — “MRI is particularly useful in differentiating TIPIC syndrome from intramural hematoma or carotid dissection, that are the principal vascular differential diagnoses.” 3. Carotid thrombosis was excluded — “On Doppler studies, the affected carotid artery on the right side demonstrated normal flow parameters.” 4. Neck abscess and lymphadenitis were excluded — “no neck mass or cervical lymphadenopathy was noted.” 5. Thyroiditis was excluded — “The thyroid gland, parathyroid glands and salivary glands were normal.” 6. Migraine was excluded — “Patient denied history of migraine or other neurological symptoms.” 7. Other vascular and non-vascular causes were systematically excluded by imaging — “The diagnosis of TIPIC syndrome requires imaging evidence of the exclusion of other vascular and non-vascular causes of neck pain.”

selection.dx_key: transient perivascular inflammation of the carotid artery
selection.screen_reason: Unilateral tender carotid bifurcation pain with perivascular enhancing tissue and no stenosis or dissection is classic TIPIC syndrome.
selection.second_look_note: Focal pain and tenderness over the carotid bifurcation after a mild febrile prodrome with perivascular enhancing tissue and no stenosis or dissection gives TIPIC syndrome.
